verdict: Robinhood swung back into profit in Q4 2023 — $30M of net income on $471M of revenue — as high interest rates lifted net interest revenue 41% and crypto trading recovered.

kpis.label: Net income
kpis.note: vs a $166M loss a year ago

segments.name: Transaction-based revenues
segments.note: Fees from customers' trades — crypto $43M, options $121M, equities $25M and $11M of other trading fees. Crypto rose 10% as digital-asset markets recovered.

segments.name: Net interest revenues
segments.note: Interest on customers' cash and margin loans, plus securities lending, less interest paid on customer balances — up on bigger balances and higher short-term interest rates.

segments.name: Other revenues
segments.note: Mostly Robinhood Gold subscriptions — 1.42M subscribers, up 25% — plus Sherwood Media.

opex.name: Operations
opex.note: Customer support and running the service.

opex.name: Provision for credit losses
opex.note: Money set aside for customer loans that may not be repaid.

opex.name: Marketing
opex.note: Advertising and promotions to win new customers — up 48%.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Legal, finance and head office — down 32% as one-off costs faded.

takeaways.title: Interest became the biggest line
takeaways.text: Net interest revenues rose 41% year-over-year to $236M — more than trading fees — driven by growth in interest-earning assets and higher short-term interest rates.

takeaways.title: Back in the black
takeaways.text: Net income was $30M versus a $166M loss a year ago. Total operating expenses fell 17% to $445M, and the tax line was a $1M benefit, so profit came out slightly above the $29M pre-tax figure.

takeaways.title: Customer assets jumped 65%
takeaways.text: Assets under custody rose 65% year-over-year to $102.6B on $4.6B of net deposits and higher market values. Gold subscribers rose 25% to 1.42M and funded customers reached 23.4M.

otherDetail: Other income, net was $3M — small next to the main business. Income tax was a $1M benefit rather than a bill, which is why net income ($30M) sits slightly above pre-tax income ($29M).
footerNote: Robinhood does not report a separate cost of revenue; 'Brokerage and transaction' — the direct cost of executing customers' trades — is shown as the direct cost here. Expense lines are as re-presented in Robinhood's Q4 2024 earnings release, which splits the original $40M operations line into Operations ($26M) and Provision for credit losses ($14M).

sources.label: Q4 2024 earnings release — re-presented 2023 comparatives (SEC EDGAR)
